# offline wiki snapshot 20260817 via the `osrs-cache` MCP `get_wiki_sections` + `get_wiki_section`.
# Companion to `impling-loot.tsv` (baby, young, gourmet, earth, essence, eclectic); same schema,
# same conventions. Each impling was read from BOTH pages - the creature page and the jar item
# page - and reconciled. They agree on every item, quantity and rarity for all six. The ONLY
# difference anywhere is row ORDER, on magpie: the creature page lists the eight noted rows first
# (Runite bar, Diamond, Diamond amulet, Amulet of power, Ring of life, Ring of forging, Ring of
# recoil after Black dragonhide), the jar page interleaves them. Same 20 items, same rates, same
# stack sizes on both. No value disagreement on any of the six.
# All twelve pages carry the banner "The following drop rates are provided by Jagex, unless
# otherwise specified." - these are authoritative published rates, not community drop-log
# Provenance oldids (creature page / jar item page):

# METHOD NOTE: the derived retrieval text the MCP returns was cross-checked against the lossless
# Parsoid HTML in `wiki.sqlite` (`pages.raw_content_zstd`, zstd streaming decompress) by counting
# <tr> in every `item-drops` table. Counts match exactly and nothing was dropped:
#   nature 19 main + 1 tertiary;   nature jar 1 jar-return + 19 main + 1 tertiary;
#   magpie 20 + 1;  ninja 19 + 1;  crystal 18 + 2;  dragon 19 + 1;  lucky 5 main, no tertiary.
# The rows below are generated FROM that raw HTML, not from the derived text. The sqlite `chunks`
# table was NOT used - it stores truncated rendered text.
# SECTION VALUES: `main` and `tertiary` only. No `preroll` in this batch - gourmet's Grubby key is
# the only pre-roll among the twelve implings.
# MAIN-TABLE RARITY SUMS - every one of the six sums to exactly 1:
# Tertiary rows are independent rolls and are excluded from those sums by design.
# Magpie's Black dragonhide is printed as `2/21`, not reduced - kept verbatim, and it is what
# makes the 20-row table sum to 1 over 21 slots.
# LUCKY IS NOT AN ORDINARY ITEM TABLE and has been encoded verbatim rather than forced into one.
# The wiki publishes five rows whose Item cells read "Roll from easy clue table", "... medium ...",
# "... hard ...", "... elite ...", "... master ...", each 1/5, quantity 1. Prose on both pages
# (oldid 15297402 / 15187655): "Looting a lucky impling gives players one roll on the drop table of
# an easy, medium, hard, elite, or master clue scroll. There is an equal chance of rolling into
# each tier's clue scroll table." Sourced to Mod Ash, 1 October 2016: "It rolls the easy, medium,
# hard, elite or master clue lists with equal chance of each."
#   - The five rows are kept as published, in the `main` section, at 1/5 each. They sum to 1.
#   - Their `obj` cells are EMPTY. A row here names a TABLE, not an item, so there is no item
#     behind it - the same rule the first batch applied to baby's `Nothing` row. The wiki
#     illustrates each row with the tier's reward-casket icon; for reference those caskets are
#     obj.trail_reward_casket_easy / _medium / _hard / _elite / _master, but a lucky impling does
#     NOT grant a casket, so naming one in the obj column would be wrong.
#   - CAVEAT ON THE MASTER ROW, published on both pages: "Although looting a lucky impling has a
#     chance of rolling the master clue scroll table, it is not possible to receive a bloodhound
#     pet when doing so. Similarly, it is not possible to receive a master clue scroll as a result
#     of opening a lucky impling jar." Mod Ash, 7 April 2019: "[Would it be possible to get a
#     master clue scroll from a lucky imp since they give a random clue reward?] I'm afraid that -
#     and the dog - are not on their list as far as I know."
#   - Lucky has NO tertiary table at all - the only one of the twelve implings without one.
# CRYSTAL is Prifddinas-only and structurally the odd one of the remaining five. Confirmed from

# spawns within Prifddinas. One may be found at a time on each world, respawning at :00 and :30,

#   - 13 of its 18 main rows are variable stacks; the other tables are mostly fixed quantities.
# Its page also has no "Rarity" section and its Loot prose omits the per-clue profit line the
# other pages carry. Neither affects the table.
# DRAGON has two rows the reader should not mistake for errors:
#   - `Dragonstone bolt tips` appears TWICE, both at 1/19: once as 10-30 and once as a flat 36.

#   - `Dragon javelin tips` (25-35, 1/19) carries footnote [d 1]: "Only dropped after completion

#     table if you can't have that one." This schema has no conditional column, so the row is
